page: Vultr vcg-l40s-16c-180g-48vram is a Cloud GPU server powered by an Intel Xeon 6448H processor with 16 physical cores and 16 vCPUs on an x86_64 architecture. The CPU operates at a base clock speed of 2.0 GHz and features a shared allocation model. The system is equipped with 180.0 GB of system memory, providing 11.25 GB per core. For acceleration, it includes a single NVIDIA L40S GPU from the Ada Lovelace family with 48 GB of dedicated VRAM. Local storage consists of a 1200 GB NVMe SSD, and the server includes one complimentary public IPv4 address.

Benchmark results show top-tier performance in specific workloads, particularly LLM inference. For a small 135M model, prompt processing reaches 13631.52 tokens per second and text generation reaches 610.8 tokens per second. For a medium 7B model, prompt processing registers at 6293.73 tokens per second and text generation at 153.1 tokens per second. Single-threaded gzip compression and bzip3 decompression also rank in the top tier, achieving 35.53 GB/sec and 15.59 GB/sec respectively. General CPU and memory benchmarks, such as stress-ng and PassMark, fall into the average category, reflecting the shared CPU allocation.

The server offers high resource density by pairing a high-capacity 48 GB VRAM GPU with 180 GB of system memory, making it qualitatively cost-efficient for memory-intensive AI workloads. However, the shared CPU allocation model presents a potential performance tradeoff for CPU-bound tasks, as reflected in the average multi-core stress-ng and PassMark scores. This configuration is highly suited for LLM inference, machine learning model execution, data science pipelines, and GPU-accelerated database operations.
